bull.b: A roughly 20% U.S. dollar share gives Celsius meaningful scale in energy drinks, while higher sales productivity per distribution point suggests stronger retail execution. Together, these factors can support durable shelf relevance and improve growth quality as distribution is optimized.

Robust operating and free cash flow indicate that Celsius is converting its earnings into internally generated funding. This supports continued brand investment, manufacturing expansion and shareholder returns while providing an important source of financial flexibility over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Alani Nu provides high-growth portfolio diversification
bull.b: Alani Nu is adding a rapidly scaling growth engine alongside the CELSIUS brand, broadening the portfolio and supporting consolidated expansion. Its strong retail performance and limited-time-offer traction can improve brand diversification and create additional opportunities for cross-portfolio growth.

bear.b: The sharp rise in debt-to-equity materially reduces Celsius’s financial flexibility compared with prior years. Although equity remains positive, higher leverage can absorb more cash through financing obligations and leave less capacity to manage sustained margin pressure or fund expansion internally.

Recent profitability is materially less stable than in earlier periods, with net margin compression occurring despite positive gross and operating margins. Persistent commodity and freight pressure, together with promotional investment, could limit operating leverage and weaken the durability of future earnings growth.

The core CELSIUS brand is facing a meaningful sales decline while SKU changes and inventory normalization continue. Retail availability, assortment decisions and shipment execution therefore remain important recovery dependencies, making consolidated growth more reliant on successful integration and portfolio performance.
